citation: Richards, "Arithmetic Operations in Digital Computers", Van Nostrand, 1955
title: Arithmetic Operations in Digital Computers

segments.title: Front matter
segments.why: The section is front matter rather than arithmetic-unit design content.

segments.title: Symbolic Representation of Quantities
segments.why: The chapter discusses number representations without describing a covered arithmetic-unit mechanism.

segments.title: Boolean Algebra Applied to Computer Components
segments.why: The chapter presents general Boolean algebra and switching-circuit synthesis rather than arithmetic-unit architectures.

segments.title: Switching Networks
segments.why: The chapter covers general switching networks and components rather than a specific arithmetic-unit mechanism.

segments.title: Binary Addition and Subtraction
segments.why: The chapter describes binary adder/subtracter organizations, carry propagation and acceleration, complement recirculation, and carry-completion operation.

segments.title: Binary Multiplication and Division
segments.why: The chapter describes partial-product multiplication and iterative binary division mechanisms.

segments.title: Decimal Codes
segments.why: The chapter classifies decimal digit representations without describing an arithmetic unit or conversion mechanism.

segments.title: Counting, Binary and Decimal
segments.why: The chapter describes binary and decimal counter structures that implement repeated increment operations.

segments.title: Decimal Addition and Subtraction
segments.why: The chapter develops decimal adders and subtracters for binary-coded decimal digits, including 8421 correction logic.

segments.title: Decimal Multiplication and Division
segments.why: The chapter compares digit-at-a-time decimal multiplication and division mechanisms with speed-oriented refinements.

segments.title: Miscellaneous Operations
segments.why: The chapter describes fixed-iteration procedures for converting values between decimal and binary representations.

segments.title: Computer Organization and Control
segments.why: The chapter concerns computer organization, sequencing, and control rather than arithmetic-unit mechanisms.

segments.title: Programming
segments.why: The chapter concerns stored-program programming methods rather than arithmetic-unit hardware.

segments.title: Bibliography and Index
segments.why: The section is bibliography and index material rather than design content.
